bib.title: Branch-Train-MiX: Mixing Expert LLMs into a Mixture-of-Experts LLM

question: How can an LLM be given several specialised domain capabilities cheaply, combining the parallel training of Branch-Train-Merge with a single unified Mixture-of-Experts model?
hypothesis: Even a small amount of combined MoE finetuning after independent expert training and merging can give large improvements, and learned token-level routing beats BTM's input-level expert selection.
contributions: BTX: branch seed LLM, train experts in parallel, mix FF layers as MoE experts, average other params, finetune router
BTX generalises Branch-Train-Merge (no MoE finetune) and sparse upcycling (no expert training)
Best accuracy-efficiency tradeoff versus dense, BTM and sparse upcycling baselines

method.summary: Copy Llama-2 7B three times and continue pretraining on math, code and Wikipedia data independently. Combine the feedforward layers of the three experts plus the original seed as four MoE experts per layer, average attention and other parameters, add a randomly initialised linear router per layer, then finetune the whole MoE on the mixed data for 80B tokens.
method.task: continued pretraining of a pretrained LLM for multi-domain capability (MoE upcycling)

models.name: BTX Top-2
models.architecture: Llama-2 7B with 4-expert MoE feedforward per layer, Top-2 routing
models.init_from: Llama-2 7B expert LLMs (math, code, Wikipedia, seed)

models.name: Llama-2 13B, CodeLlama 7B, Llemma 7B, Dense, Sparse upcycling, BTM

training.objective: language modelling NLL for experts; NLL plus load-balancing loss L_LB = alpha*N*sum u_i p_i for MoE stage
training.steps: experts 48k (math), 50k (code); MoE stage not stated in steps
training.tokens: experts 201B math, 210B code, 42B Wikipedia; MoE finetune 80B (Top-2), 160B for Sample Top-1 at equal compute
training.regularisation: load balancing alpha=0.01 for default Top-2
training.compute: BTX 926.1 GPU-days total; sparse upcycling (CM) 1007.1 GPU-days (Table 3)
training.wall_clock: BTX 7.8 days, sparse upcycling CM 7.9 days (Table 3)

other.sample_top1_temperature: tau=max(0.5,-rt), r=1e-4, t training steps; first layer uses soft routing
other.same_hparams: same optimiser hyperparameters for baselines, experts and MoE models
other.moe_share_of_compute: 23% for BTX, 100% for sparse upcycling CM

inference.samples: single greedy run; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero- or few-shot: GSM8K 8-shot, MATH 4-shot, HumanEval 0-shot, MBPP 3-shot, NQ 5-shot, TriviaQA 5-shot, reasoning 0-shot, MMLU 5-shot

parameters.BTM expert selection: tf-idf cosine similarity to mean tf-idf embedding of each expert's training data, Top-k experts (Top-1 or Top-2)

eval.protocol: Domain scores are averages: math = GSM8K and MATH, code = HumanEval and MBPP, knowledge = NQ and TriviaQA, reasoning = ARC-E, ARC-C, SIQA, PIQA, WinoGrande. No seeds or significance tests.

limits: Only three domains and four experts tried due to compute limits.
Simple MoE implementation, experts not placed on separate GPUs; efficiency gains unoptimised.
Compared only to BTM (0% MoE compute) and sparse upcycling (100% MoE compute); no sweep of compute allocation ratio.
Only uniform mixture sampling for MoE finetuning tested.
Instruction finetuning and RLHF of the BTX model are left for future work; the paper covers pretraining only.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; single Llama-2 7B scale; no code or weights released per text.
Hardware (GPU type and count) not stated.

code.snippet: FF_MoE^l(x) = sum_{i=1..N} g_i(W^l x) FF_i^l(x); g(W^l x) = SoftMax(TopK(W^l x))
L_LB = alpha N sum_i u_i p_i, u_i = (1/|B|) sum_{x in B} g_i(W^l x), p_i = (1/|B|) sum_{x in B} SoftMax_i(W^l x)
